name: Russia
summary_text: Russia presents severe legal and physical risks for transgender visitors, and the situation has deteriorated sharply since 2022. Legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care were banned outright in 2023; the Supreme Court has designated the "international LGBT movement" an extremist organisation; and the expanded "propaganda" law criminalises any public expression — including, explicitly, anything "justifying" gender transition. Foreigners who violate these laws face arrest, up to 15 days' detention, and deportation, and the US State Department explicitly warns LGBT travellers of this. The UK Home Office assesses that trans people specifically are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution in Russia. Enforcement has produced over a hundred "extremism" convictions for displaying LGBT symbols or participation, bar raids, and the death in custody of a man who ran travel tours for gay customers. Enforcement focuses on public expression and activism rather than private existence, and same-sex activity itself is not criminalised — a discreet visitor is not automatically targeted — but there is effectively no police protection, and detention carries placement by passport sex. Chechnya and the wider North Caucasus, where quasi-Sharia governance applies, are in a separate and graver category of danger for anyone perceived as LGBT.

sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office CPIN Russia: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (June 2025, updated Aug 2026): official country-of-origin information and assessment for asylum claims - the 'gay propaganda' laws, the 'extremist' designation of the 'international LGBT movement', the ban on legal/medical transition, and risk assessment.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying US State Department travel advisory for Russia (Level 4 'Do Not Travel') includes warnings relevant to LGBT travellers.

sources.title: Russia: Rising Toll of LGBT ‘Extremism’ Designation | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jun 2025): 'Russia: Rising Toll of LGBT ‘Extremism’ Designation' — documents raids, prosecutions and violence against LGBT people since the 'international LGBT public movement' was designated extremist.

sources.title: ‘What even is propaganda?’. How Russia’s murky anti-LGBTQ laws fuel a repressive campaign that makes the state millions — Meduza
sources.claim_summary: Meduza feature (June 2025): 'What even is propaganda?' - how Russia's murky anti-LGBTQ laws fuel a repressive campaign that makes the state millions; cases under the 'LGBT propaganda' laws grew eighteenfold over a decade; fines in the past two years brought over 60 million rubles into state coffers; traces the law's evolution from 2013 (minors) to the December 2022 all-ages expansion.

sources.title: ‘You’re a Second-Class Citizen’: Arrests, Club Raids and Extremism Charges Define LGBTQ+ Life in Russia in 2025 - The Moscow Times
sources.claim_summary: The Moscow Times (June 2025): 'You're a second-class citizen' - arrests, club raids and extremism charges define LGBTQ life in Russia in 2025; since the Supreme Court declared the 'international LGBT movement' extremist, any public display of queerness (a rainbow badge, a photo with a same-sex partner, even a book) can be interpreted as extremist; unclear boundaries drive people to hide entirely.

AP (Dec 2024): 'Russian man arrested for allegedly running LGBTQ+ travel agency found dead in custody' — detained on extremism-related charges over an LGBTQ+ travel business, found dead in a pretrial detention facility.

AP (Dec 2024): 'Russia's LGBTQ+ community is living in fear following new laws and court rulings, activists say' — the post-designation crackdown under Putin pushes people into silence, flight and self-censorship.

sources.title: Russia's New Queer Purge: The Court Decision Driving the LGBT Community Into Exile
sources.claim_summary: Foreign Policy (Aug 2024): 'Russia's New Queer Purge: The Court Decision Driving the LGBT Community Into Exile' — how the extremism designation fuelled a purge and mass emigration of LGBT Russians.

sources.title: Trans in Russia: Tricked into conversion therapy in Siberia
sources.claim_summary: BBC Russian investigation (July 2024): 'Tricked into conversion therapy in Russia for being trans' - Ada, 23, was deceived into a Siberian 'conversion therapy centre' where she was held for nine months, forced to take testosterone, pray and do manual labour, and told to castrate a pig to 'understand what castration means'; she escaped after nine months.

sources.title: In limbo. For many transgender Russians, emigration is the only means of survival — Novaya Gazeta Europe
sources.claim_summary: Novaya Gazeta Europe (June 2024): 'In limbo' - for many transgender Russians, emigration is the only means of survival after the law prohibiting gender-reassignment surgery and legal gender change; in 2023 one in three trans Russians said they had been threatened with physical violence (Coming Out/Sphere Foundation study).

sources.title: ‘I will pretend not to be me’: Russia cracks down on LGBTQ+ community | LGBTQ+ rights | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (Jan 2024): 'I will pretend not to be me' - Russia cracks down on the LGBTQ+ community; features queer performance artist Gena Marvin (documentary Queendom) challenging the Putin regime's gender norms through public performances.
